_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY — do not use as-is. Run `uv run python setup_wizard.py` to generate a real config.json for YOUR Housecall Pro account. The hcp_id and pipeline-stage id values below are fake; real ones are unique per account, so a config copied between accounts matches nothing and every capacity/pipeline tool silently returns empty. Run `hcp_check_setup` in Claude to confirm your config matches your account.

scheduling.notes: productive_hours_per_day is real working capacity. appointment_window_hours is the window you block on the calendar, including the unpaid break. The DIFFERENCE between them (here 0.5h = 30 min) is subtracted from any day of 6h or more when computing actual worked hours. Set these to match how you actually book days.
scheduling.blended_cost_note: Fully-loaded cost per tech-hour: wages, payroll burden, vehicle, insurance, overhead. This drives every margin number, so use YOUR figure — 95.0 is a placeholder.
scheduling._tuning_notes: Optional. full_day_min_hours: shortest day that gets a break deducted. anchor_tolerance_hours: how far started_at may sit from the scheduled start and still be trusted. early_finish_tolerance_hours: how early completed_at may be and still count as a real early finish (finishing early is real signal; finishing 'late' past the tolerance is usually paperwork after leaving site). cluster_gap_days: gap within which two jobs for the same customer+address are treated as one split project. Defaults are fine unless your crews work unusual patterns.

team.name: Example Lead Tech
team.notes: Full-time field tech. Counts 1.0x toward capacity.

team.name: Example Apprentice
team.notes: Counts 0.5x toward capacity but can still be booked a full day.

team.name: Example Owner
team.notes: Sales and estimating only. field_tech false keeps them out of capacity math.

job_pipeline_stages.name: New Job
job_pipeline_stages.notes: Get your real stages by asking Claude to run hcp_get_pipeline_statuses, or let setup_wizard.py fill them in.

tags._comment: Optional. A job-tag convention the scheduling tools understand. This is one franchise's system — adopt, change, or delete it. Tools degrade gracefully when tags are absent; they just flag jobs as untagged.

known_quirks: Dollar amounts are integers in CENTS — divide by 100 to display.
Line items endpoint returns {object, data, url} — read 'data', not 'line_items'.
Job date filters are scheduled_start_min / scheduled_start_max and REQUIRE a trailing Z on the timestamp.

work_status filter values (unscheduled/scheduled/in_progress/completed/canceled) differ from the display strings the API returns ('needs scheduling', 'in progress', 'complete rated', ...). The filter must be sent as an array.

Job and Estimate schedule objects use scheduled_start/scheduled_end/arrival_window. Appointment and Event objects use start_time/end_time/arrival_window_minutes. Mixing them up renders '?' rather than erroring.
Only started_at/completed_at exist on work_timestamps — there is no per-tech time tracking and no pause data in the public API.
/api/price_book/services returns service_materials and service_labor_rates as empty arrays unless you pass expand[].
Canceled jobs are archived; /jobs/{id}/appointments returns HTTP 400 'Archived job' for them permanently.
Fanning out more than ~90 concurrent job sub-requests draws HTTP 429. Never treat a failed fetch as an empty payload — it silently becomes '0 quoted hours'.
